name: Dinah
description: Jacob's daughter living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: Dinah went out to see the daughters of the land, and Shechem saw her, took her, and defiled her. It sounds romantic, he was enamoured, but what it says is he saw, took, and defiled, because evil intent drives what is done by the eyes.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

points: Dinah went out playing with the daughters of the children of the land, and a prince of the country saw her.

note.label: The 5 Signs of a Good Wife

points: Dinah, Jacob's only daughter, went out to see the daughters of the land without supervision, and Shechem the son of Hamor took her, and lay with her, and defiled her. This was stranger rape.

note.label: Genesis 34: Dinah and the Zeal of Simeon and Levi

points: His soul clave unto Dinah and he loved the damsel: the love comes after the violation. Then came more deception, the slaughter of the men of Shechem, and turmoil under Jacob. Visual attraction produced violence and bloodshed, as it still does when one man is jealous of another.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

points: Shechem's soul clave to Dinah after he defiled her; he did it backwards, taking first and loving after. That is the world's pattern, not righteousness.

note.label: Genesis 34: Dinah and the Zeal of Simeon and Levi

points: On the third day, when they were sore, two of the sons, Simeon and Levi, took each man his sword, came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males; they took Dinah out, spoiled the city, and carried away the substance and the households.

note.label: Genesis 34: Dinah and the Zeal of Simeon and Levi
